newsitem.title: ESTONIA: ESTONIA-NEWSPAPERS ANGRY OVER TOBACCO AD BAN.
newsitem.headline: ESTONIA-NEWSPAPERS ANGRY OVER TOBACCO AD BAN.

text.p: The body which represents Estonia's newspapers on Thursday said it was angered by a ban on tobacco advertising.
The controversial ban was part of a wide-ranging advertisement law passed by parliament on Wednesday evening which also limits the advertising of alchohol.

"The newspaper association is of the opinion that there is no need for the law in such a form. It is too regulatory and creates a huge bureaucratic supervisory apparatus, which enables officials to behave their own way," Tarmu Tammerk, managing director of the association, told Reuters.

He said the association was annoyed that a comromise proposal was not accepted, whereby tobacco advertising would have been banned in electronic and outdoor media but been allowed on the inside pages of print media.
"The newspaper association sees this as a government step against print media because it decreases advertising revenues," Tammerk added.
Kaur Hanson, chairman of advertisment company Zoom, was not upset over the law.
"It has no impact on advertisement companies financially as the money will be spent in some other way. We have to think more creatively," he said.
